name: promptwl
description: A red-team and guardrail wordlist for LLMs. SecLists, but for language models.

files.title: Instruction override
files.description: Phrases that attempt to override or supersede prior instructions.

files.title: Delimiter confusion
files.description: Markers impersonating role/turn boundaries or system framing.

files.title: Payload splitting
files.description: Instructions assembled across multiple turns, variables, or fragments to evade single-message filters.

files.title: Chat template markers
files.description: Real control markers from deployed chat templates (ChatML, Llama, Gemma, Phi, Command-R, GLM, DeepSeek, Qwen, plain-text templates) that untrusted content can forge.

files.title: Persona override
files.description: Role-play framings that swap the model into an unrestricted persona.

files.title: Refusal suppression
files.description: Phrases pressuring the model not to refuse or to drop caveats.

files.title: Hypothetical / fictional framing
files.description: Fictional, academic, or hypothetical wrappers used to try to bypass refusal behavior.

files.title: Authority impersonation
files.description: Claims of developer/admin/special authorization used to pressure the model into dropping constraints.

files.title: Dual response & divider
files.description: Patterns that splice a refusal and an unrestricted continuation into one answer, with a divider between them.

files.title: Attribute / config override
files.description: Structured key:value style attempts to flip a safety setting (redactions, filters, refusal mode) from inside message content.

files.title: System prompt leak
files.description: Probes that attempt to reveal the hidden system prompt or config.

files.title: Training data extraction
files.description: Probes that try to elicit memorized training data, verbatim copyrighted text, or personal data.

files.title: Sensitive data disclosure
files.description: Probes that ask for secrets, credentials, personal data, or internal context the application placed in the prompt.

files.title: Encoding & obfuscation
files.description: Cues that a payload is smuggled via encoding, homoglyphs, or spacing.

files.title: Invisible characters
files.description: Zero-width and Unicode Tags codepoints used for ASCII smuggling.

files.title: Language switching
files.description: Cues that a payload is smuggled via translation, code-switching, or a low-resource language.

files.title: Steganographic channels
files.description: Codepoint channels that carry a payload outside the words — variation selectors, Hangul fillers, combining marks, Braille dot patterns, emoji modifiers.

files.title: Classifier-evasion paraphrase
files.description: Requests to reword a payload so an automated classifier — not a human — stops detecting it. Meaning preserved, surface changed.

files.title: Token-level substitution
files.description: Instructions to rewrite text at the token level (phonetic respelling, invented words, emoji letters, affix padding) so it stops matching filters and tokenizers.

files.title: Tool & RAG injection
files.description: Indirect-injection phrases planted in docs, tool output, web pages, or email.

files.title: Memory & session poisoning
files.description: Patterns aimed at agents with persistent memory, trying to plant instructions that survive into future sessions.

files.title: Tool argument injection
files.description: Patterns that steer the arguments of a legitimate tool call (URL, recipient, query, parameters) from inside untrusted content.

files.title: Spanish (es)
files.description: Core override/jailbreak patterns in Spanish.

files.title: French (fr)
files.description: Core override/jailbreak patterns in French.

files.description: Core override/jailbreak patterns in German.

files.description: Core override/jailbreak patterns in Portuguese.

files.description: Core override/jailbreak patterns in Italian.

files.title: Russian (ru)
files.description: Core override/jailbreak patterns in Russian.

files.title: Chinese (zh)
files.description: Core override/jailbreak patterns in Simplified Chinese.

files.title: Arabic (ar)
files.description: Core override/jailbreak patterns in Arabic.

files.title: Hindi (hi)
files.description: Core override/jailbreak patterns in Hindi.

files.title: Japanese (ja)
files.description: Core override/jailbreak patterns in Japanese.

files.title: Image & file injection
files.description: Instructions hidden in non-text channels (image text, alt-text, metadata, document layers) read by multimodal pipelines.

files.title: Markdown & HTML injection
files.description: Output-channel payloads that break the renderer displaying a model's answer (HTML/Markdown/CSV breakout) — the output side of the trust boundary.

files.title: Anomalous / glitch tokens
files.description: Publicly-known glitch tokens for tokenizer/model robustness testing.

files.title: Control characters & encoding artifacts
files.description: Control characters, zero-width/bidi, and BPE residue strings known to trigger anomalous model behavior.

files.title: Fragmentation base words
files.description: Seed words the cross-tokenizer probe fragments to measure how tokenizers segment the variants.

files.title: Boundary separators
files.description: Real, exotic, and invisible separator codepoints that shift apparent token boundaries.

files.title: Unicode confusables
files.description: Confusable character pair table (UTS-39) and confusable-substituted attack keywords for homoglyph filter-bypass testing.
files.scan_note: UTS-39 look-alike test vectors — they fold to ordinary words, so they are test inputs, not scan patterns.

files.title: Encoding chain patterns
files.description: Catalog of single- and multi-layer encoding chain patterns (leet, base64, rot13, reverse, and combinations) used to evade keyword filters; includes known-residual cases requiring semantic defense.
files.scan_note: encoding-chain names and seed phrases — probe vocabulary, not scan patterns.

files.title: Unknowable probes
files.description: Questions with no determinate answer, where the failure mode is confident fabrication rather than refusal — plus pressure to answer anyway.
